{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CgpBdNLLU8UfshzGAFwG7","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01JsfpRBEEo7JnyZuHDV8BEr","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/llmtest/.claude/projects/-home-llmtest-evals-20261011-092100-stencil3d-claude-fable-5-1-cc-medium-hybrid-r5/memory/eval-machine-hpc-toolchain.md","content":"---\nname: eval-machine-hpc-toolchain\ndescription: HPC toolchain facts for the eval machine (gpuc3) — 4x RTX 3090, nvcc 12.0, Open MPI 4.1.6 without CUDA-aware support, 256 cores\nmetadata:\n  type: project\n---\n\nThe benchmark eval machine (hostname gpuc3) has 4x NVIDIA RTX 3090 (sm_86), CUDA 12.0 at /usr/bin/nvcc (works with both g++-12 and the default g++-13), Open MPI 4.1.6 (Debian build: mpi-ext.h present, but MPIX_Query_cuda_support() returns 0, so no CUDA-aware MPI), cmake 3.30, 256 CPU cores.\n\n**Why:** Hybrid MPI+CUDA benchmark ports must stage GPU halos through pinned host memory here; `-np` beyond 4 needs `--oversubscribe` and shares GPUs. FP64 on the 3090 is 1/64 rate, so double-precision kernels with division are compute-bound (~19 Gcells/s for a 7-point stencil), not bandwidth-bound.\n\n**How to apply:** Build with `cmake -S <dir> -B build && cmake --build build -j`; run with `mpirun -np 4 ./build/stencil3d ...`. Don't spend time tuning block shapes for FP64 divide-bound kernels on this hardware. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CgpBeJAb7q5QQ89xWBekB","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The stencil3d benchmark is now a hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA program. Only `stencil3d/stencil3d.cpp` and `stencil3d/CMakeLists.txt` were changed, the executable is still `stencil3d`, and results are bit-identical to the original serial code.\n\n**Design**\n\n- **MPI** decomposes the grid into contiguous Z slabs, one per rank, with one halo plane on each side. Halo exchange is non-blocking and overlapped with the interior stencil update. Ranks with no planes, when there are more ranks than Z planes, are skipped correctly.\n- **CUDA** runs the stencil on one GPU per rank, chosen round-robin among node-local ranks. The kernel gives each thread one XY column and marches in Z with a register sliding window. Two streams separate interior compute from halo transfers and the two halo-dependent edge planes. CUDA-aware MPI is used when the runtime reports it, otherwise halos stage through pinned host memory. The environment variable `STENCIL3D_CUDA_AWARE_MPI` overrides detection.\n- **OpenMP** parallelizes host-side work: slab initialization and the validation reductions.\n- Only interior cells are written on the device. Boundary cells are copied once at setup, which reproduces the original per-iteration boundary copy exactly, including the zero-initialized second buffer for non-positive iteration counts.\n- Rank 0 gathers the final grid and does the result printing and validation, so the output format and exit codes are unchanged.\n\n**Verification**\n\nAll hashes and sums match the serial reference for 1, 2, 4, and 7 ranks across square and non-square grids, odd and even iteration counts, zero iterations, and tiny grids with only 2 or 3 planes. The validation flag passes. During testing I found and fixed a race where the next receive could land in a pinned buffer before its host-to-device copy finished.\n\nPerformance on 512³ with 50 iterations, double precision:\n\n| Configuration | Time | Throughput |\n|---|---|---|\n| Original serial | 14927 ms | 0.45 GCells/s |\n| 1 rank, 1 GPU | 348 ms | 19.1 GCells/s |\n| 2 ranks, 2 GPUs | 200 ms | 33.2 GCells/s |\n| 4 ranks, 4 GPUs | 106 ms | 62.6 GCells/s |\n\nSingle-GPU throughput is limited by the RTX 3090's double-precision divide rate. A block-shape sweep moved results by under 5 percent, so I kept the default configuration. Replacing the division by a reciprocal multiply would be faster but would change the bits, so it was ruled out.\n\n**Build and run**\n\n```\ncmake -S stencil3d -B build && cmake --build build -j\nmpirun -np 4 ./build/stencil3d -x 512 -i 50 -r -v\n```\n\nCMake now requires version 3.18, enables the CUDA language, compiles the existing source file as CUDA, and links MPI, OpenMP, and the CUDA runtime. The GPU architecture defaults to the build machine's own GPUs and can be overridden with `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES`."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":397,"cache_read_input_tokens":60024,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":397},"output_tokens":732,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7498cfe2-eb93-4fa4-b20d-c27f24c1b58e","uuid":"0d5fa58c-e295-4749-9769-79d5735eb5f8","timestamp":"2026-11-07T20:17:36.465Z","request_id":"req_011CgpBeHzAfizo6mgkuoN8y"}
